items.claim: Claude Code v2.1.307 adds /claude-api api-version, which moves code to Anthropic API version 2026-10-21. That version removes temperature, top_p and top_k, which now return a 400 error on every model.
items.why_it_matters: Code that still sends sampling parameters will break once it moves to the new anthropic-version header. The new command is meant to help with that migration.
items.try_this: Before changing the anthropic-version header to 2026-10-21, search your code for temperature, top_p and top_k and read the official migration guide.

verification.method: Read the GitHub release notes and Anthropic's API versions page, which lists 2026-10-21 and the removed parameters.

items.excerpt: Added /claude-api api-version to move Claude API code to API version 2026-10-21

items.claim: Anthropic announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards: free misuse monitoring that keeps activity data in the customer's own cloud storage. It rolls out in phases later this fall, and eligible customers get ZDR on Fable 5 and 5.1 until then.
items.why_it_matters: Regulated teams blocked by 30-day retention on Fable 5 may get a path to frontier models without Anthropic holding their data.
items.try_this: If 30-day retention kept your organization off Fable 5, request access through the form on the announcement page and ask whether you qualify for interim ZDR.

verification.method: Anthropic's announcement page confirms the free pricing, customer-owned storage, phased rollout and the interim ZDR offer. Not yet generally available.

items.excerpt: Anthropic doesn't charge for Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.

items.claim: IBM released granite-speech-5.0-2b under Apache 2.0. It does ASR in six languages, translates to and from English, and accepts keyword-biasing lists of up to 2,000 terms.
items.why_it_matters: This is an open speech model you can steer toward product names and acronyms, a common failure point in voice-agent transcription.
items.try_this: Test granite-speech-5.0-2b from its Hugging Face card on a sample of your own audio, with and without a keyword list of your domain terms.

verification.method: The model card confirms Apache 2.0, six ASR languages and the 2,000-term keyword limit. The #2 WER leaderboard rank was not checked.

items.claim: Claude Code mods are plugins made of JS/TS event handlers that run inside Claude Code. Six are built in, including you-should-know, which is off by default. Mods are not sandboxed.
items.why_it_matters: You can reshape your agent's interface and intercept its tool calls. Any third-party mod runs with your full permissions and can see your secrets.
items.try_this: Before installing a third-party mod, run claude plugin validate on its directory and read the hooks: and calls: lines.

verification.method: The Claude Code mods overview docs confirm the definition, the six built-ins, that you-should-know is off by default, and that mods are not sandboxed.

items.claim: NVIDIA released Kumo Relational, a pretrained model that makes predictions straight from multi-table databases using in-context examples, with no task-specific training. Code is Apache 2.0 and weights use OpenMDW 1.1.
items.why_it_matters: This could replace feature engineering plus XGBoost for churn or demand prediction, and agents can call it through a query language.
items.try_this: Read the quickstart notebook in NVIDIA/structured-data-models-client and compare the model against your current baseline on one held-out task.

verification.method: The model card and GitHub repo exist with the stated licenses and library. The claim of beating supervised baselines on 41 tasks is NVIDIA's own (vendor claim).

items.claim: IBM published granite-timeseries-ensemble-r1, an Apache 2.0 recipe that pools four Granite time-series models into one zero-shot forecaster returning median and quantile forecasts, with no fitted weights.
items.why_it_matters: It is a reasonable default when you don't know which pretrained forecaster suits your data. IBM itself says the accuracy gain over the best member is small.
items.try_this: Backtest the ensemble against PatchTST-FM-r2 alone on your own historical windows, and check 0.1 to 0.9 interval coverage.

verification.method: The model card confirms the recipe, license and four members. The card says granite-tsfm>=0.3.10 and the blog says >=0.3.11. GIFT-Eval figures differ by snapshot date.

items.claim: OpenAI says its frontier models and Codex workflows are coming to Google Cloud through Model Garden and Google Cloud Marketplace.
items.why_it_matters: Teams standardized on Google Cloud might use OpenAI models under existing billing and procurement. Timing and model list are unconfirmed.

verification.method: OpenAI's feed confirms the announcement exists. The article returned 403, and no Google Cloud docs page confirming availability was found.

items.claim: Anthropic reports that open-weight GLM-5.3 built end-to-end V8 exploits in 50 of 410 attempts (Mythos Preview: 56). Simple bypasses got it to engage with malicious requests 64% to 100% of the time.
items.why_it_matters: Strong exploit-building ability is now downloadable with weak refusals. Defenders should assume attackers have it.
items.try_this: If you self-host open-weight models in agent pipelines, do not rely on the model's own refusals. Enforce sandboxing and tool permissions outside the model.

verification.method: The GLM-5.3 open-weight model card exists on Hugging Face. The exploit and bypass numbers are Anthropic's own evaluations, not replicated.

items.excerpt: GLM-5.3 develops end-to-end exploits in 50 of 410 attempts.

items.claim: Anthropic says Fable 5.1 in Claude Science computed the nine-loop six-particle amplitude in planar N=4 super-Yang-Mills for about $1,000 to $2,000. Physicist Lance Dixon validated the result.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a long-running agent harness completing a fragile frontier computation with little supervision beyond "keep going".

verification.method: Read Anthropic's guest post. Dixon's validation is stated there. An arXiv search found no independent paper yet.
verification.audit_note: Anthropic page confirms Fable 5.1 in Claude Science, nine-loop six-particle planar N=4 SYM amplitude, ~$1–2k cost, Lance Dixon validation.

items.claim: Dharma-AI says that rebuilding a Qwen3-4B grader's vocabulary by token cost cut average output from 350 to 101 tokens and measured inference cost by 77%, while its quality score rose from 0.703 to 0.810.
items.why_it_matters: For narrow, high-volume fine-tuned models, the tokenizer is a cost lever. Shrinking output tokens saves several times more than shrinking input.
items.try_this: Measure what share of your serving cost comes from generated versus input tokens before choosing which side to compress.

verification.method: The authors' own blog post. The VocabX paper is unpublished and under review, so the results are unreplicated.

items.excerpt: cut measured inference cost by 77% without changing the base model
